notes: Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention: bank 'b' is rows f-j, which is the half of the breadboard shown at the top of the image (rows j-f). The resistor, LED and wire ends are all in that half.

Reading the image: the resistor spans columns 3 and 6 in row h. The green wire goes from pin 2 to column 3, row g, which shares a strip with the resistor's left lead. The LED's bent (longer) leg is in column 6 and is taken as the anode. Its straight leg is in column 8 and is taken as the cathode. The black wire goes from GND to column 8, row h.
Pin 2 is named D2 and the GND pin is named GND, matching the catalogue entry for the Vidor 4000.
The software steps (Board Manager, WiFiNINA and VidorPeripherals libraries, sketch upload) are not physical parts and are not in the graph.
The tutorial lists an 82 ohm resistor. The catalogue type is a generic resistor, so the value prop is set to 82.
